title: Training Notes on the Mortgage Loan File: The Borrower's Intent to Proceed
content:
**The rule.** On a Mortgage Loan File the borrower may indicate intent to proceed in any way — an e-sign portal acknowledgment, a signed form, or a verbal statement to the loan officer noted the same day; silence is never intent to proceed. An intent to proceed is recorded only while the loan file status is disclosed. Intent to proceed counts only if it is received no later than the end of the intent-to-proceed window that starts on the initial Loan Estimate's issued date. Business days are counted forward from the issued date of the file's initial Loan Estimate, which is day zero; an intent to proceed received on the last business day of the window still counts. The window is the program's intent-to-proceed window in business days. A business day is Monday through Friday excluding the US federal public holidays observed by the Federal Reserve Banks; Saturdays, Sundays and those holidays are skipped when counting. A timely intent to proceed moves the file to processing and stamps the file's intent-to-proceed date with the date received. When the window has passed with no intent to proceed, Larkspur is no longer bound by the Loan Estimate and the application is treated as withdrawn; a borrower who comes back afterwards starts a new application and receives a new Loan Estimate.

## Questions answered

**Does the borrower have to sign something?** No. An e-sign acknowledgment, a signed form or a verbal statement to the loan officer noted the same day are all intent to proceed. Saying nothing is not.

**From which date does the window run?** From the issued date of the initial Loan Estimate on the file, counted as day zero, as recorded in the file's disclosure history.

**Is an intent to proceed received on the last day too late?** No. With a hypothetical 10-business-day window and an initial Loan Estimate issued on a Monday, with no holidays in the period, day 10 is the Monday two weeks later; an intent to proceed received that day counts, and one received on the Tuesday after does not.

**Can an intent to proceed be recorded on a file that is still application received, or already in processing?** No. It is recorded only while the file is disclosed.

**What happens after the window passes in silence?** Larkspur is no longer bound by the Loan Estimate, the application is treated as withdrawn, and a returning borrower starts a new application and receives a new Loan Estimate.

**What does a timely intent to proceed change on the file?** The file moves to processing and its intent-to-proceed date is stamped with the date received.
